question: Should Crabbox own and release a first-party Herdr plugin plus its private CLI compatibility surface?
rationale: The implementation creates an ongoing third-party compatibility and release obligation that code review cannot infer from repository structure or green CI alone.

options.title: Sponsor First-Party Herdr
options.body: Confirm repository ownership, then require a current-main dispatcher repair, explicit compatibility policy, and inspectable Herdr smoke proof before merge.

options.title: Keep Integration External
options.body: Decline the private core adapter and host the Herdr integration externally using only supported public Crabbox commands or a separately approved generic extension seam.

recommendation.title: Sponsor First-Party Herdr
recommendation.body: Confirm repository ownership, then require a current-main dispatcher repair, explicit compatibility policy, and inspectable Herdr smoke proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history is the strongest available signal for the current CLI registry and adjacent integration architecture.
